content.title: How to watch the Masters 2026: McIlroy and Young tied ahead of Sunday’s final round
content.text: Rory McIlroy entered Saturday with an unprecedented Masters lead. He arrives Sunday without a lead of his own.In a stunning development, McIlroy lost his six-stroke lead during the third round. Augusta National’s defending champion is now tied with world No. 3 Cameron Young. Together, they’re just one stroke up on Sam Burns and two up on Shane Lowry. The crowded field of viable winners also includes superstar Scottie Scheffler and three-time Masters runner-up Justin Rose.Jim Nantz is on the mic. A gold medal, silver trophy and green jacket are all in the balance. Here’s the broadcast schedule for Sunday, complete with the updated tee times.All times ET.How to watch the Masters, Round 4 Location: Augusta National Golf Club — Augusta, Ga. Time: 2 p.m., Sunday TV: CBS Streaming: Fubo (Stream Free Now!) CBS is free over the air. All broadcasts and streams are also available on Masters.com and the Masters app.Masters TV format and Sunday broadcast coverageThe “tradition unlike any other” embraces a new age of TV and streaming.Sunday’s round is primarily on CBS from 2-7 p.m., with the earlier 12-2 p.m. window on Paramount+ and the Masters’ online landings. Nantz is the golden voice of Augusta action, now in his 38th year of CBS Masters coverage. Trevor Immelman, the tournament’s 2008 champion, is the network’s lead analyst.Your browser does not support the video tag.Now, to the different streaming destinations. Everything below is also on the Masters’ website and app, both of which are home to the green jacket ceremony at 7 p.m.“On the Range” Time: 10 a.m.-noon CBS Sports Network and Paramount+ air an early live stream from the practice range. Kelly Tilghman hosts, and she’s joined by Michael Breed, Brian Crowell, Amanda Balionis and Iona Stephen.Featured groups Time: 10:15 a.m.-7 p.m. ESPN’s app tracks four starry groups across the fourth and final round. The CBS Sports/Paramount+ booth for featured groups is Breed, Crowell, Shane Bacon, Johnson Wagner and Billy Kratzert. Prime has featured groups as well.Featured holes Time: 10:30 a.m.-6:30 p.m. The ESPN app locks in on holes 4, 5 and 6 at 10:30 a.m. ESPN has an additional stream for Nos. 15 and 16, starting at 12:30 p.m. Elsewhere, Prime Video offers its own stream of the 15th and 16th holes. CBS Sports and Paramount+ do too, with Stephen, Ned Michaels and Geoff Ogilvy on the mic.Amen Corner Time: 11:45 a.m.-6 p.m. Prime’s “Inside Amen Corner” is dedicated to Augusta’s most famous stretch of Nos. 11-13. The alt-cast is hosted by Justin Kutcher, alongside Ogilvy and Smylie Kaufman. “Inside Amen Corner” finds Prime experimenting with advanced stats and data visualizations.CBS Sports Network and Paramount+ have an Amen Corner outpost, too. That coverage is held down by Grant Boone and Mark Immelman. Never to be outdone, ESPN is watching Amen Corner as well.Round 4 tee times9:06 a.m. – Aaron Rai, Charl Schwartzel 9:17 a.m. – Gary Woodland, Kurt Kitayama 9:28 a.m. – Jon Rahm, Sergio Garcia 9:39 a.m. – Si Woo Kim, Rasmus Højgaard 9:50 a.m. – Keegan Bradley, Dustin Johnson 10:01 a.m. – Matt McCarty, Corey Conners 10:12 a.m. – Viktor Hovland, Justin Thomas 10:23 a.m. – Alex Noren, Maverick McNealy 10:45 a.m. – Adam Scott, Marco Penge 10:56 a.m. – Harris English, Samuel Stevens 11:07 a.m. – Brian Harman, Jordan Spieth 11:18 a.m. – Sungjae Im, Hideki Matsuyama 11:29 a.m. – Sepp Straka, Jacob Bridgeman 11:40 a.m. – Chris Gotterup, Kristoffer Reitan 11:51 a.m. – Michael Brennan, Max Homa 12:13 p.m. – Nick Taylor, Matt Fitzpatrick 12:24 p.m. – Ludvig Åberg, Brian Campbell 12:35 p.m. – Tyrrell Hatton, Tommy Fleetwood 12:46 p.m. – Brooks Koepka, Wyndham Clark 12:57 p.m. – Ryan Gerard, Xander Schauffele 1:08 p.m. – Jake Knapp, Ben Griffin 1:30 p.m. – Patrick Reed, Collin Morikawa 1:41 p.m. – Patrick Cantlay, Russell Henley 1:52 p.m. – Scottie Scheffler, Haotong Li 2:03 p.m. – Jason Day, Justin Rose 2:14 p.m. – Sam Burns, Shane Lowry 2:25 p.m. – Cameron Young, Rory McIlroyCurrent Masters standingsIt was a miserable moving day for the pride of Northern Ireland. McIlroy shot a lean 67 on Thursday, then improved to 65 on Friday, but he ended Saturday at a deflating 1-over 73.The bogeyed first hole portended trouble. McIlroy then stabilized, going 2 under from the second hole to the 10th … only to double bogey on No. 11 and bogey again on No. 12. He had a chance to end the day with a narrow lead, but his 22-foot birdie putt rolled just wide of the cup.In contrast, Young overwrote a poor first-round showing to approach the top of the table — 73 on Thursday, 67 on Friday and 65 on Saturday. The American has been brilliant at Amen Corner, with five birdies and nothing over par so far. Young’s career-best Masters finish was when he tied for seventh in 2023. He’s in range for a far better result come Sunday.An 11-under tie between the world’s second- and third-ranked players is certainly compelling, but McIlroy and Young have company. Burns is one stroke behind them after posting a steady 68 on Saturday (four birdies, 14 pars). The Louisianian’s highest Masters finish was also in 2023, a modest tie for 29th.Lowry is one stroke shy of Burns and two shy of the leaders. He provided the soaring highlight from Saturday — a hole-in-one on the par-3 No. 6. With that glorious ace, the Irishman became the only player ever with multiple holes-in-one at the Masters. He notched his first back in 2016 on Redbud (No. 16). To date, Lowry’s best Masters result is a tie for third in 2022.England’s Rose and Australia’s Jason Day follow Lowry at 8 under. Day elevated himself with four consecutive birdies on Nos. 12-15. Rose, who lost last year’s playoff to McIlroy, has consistent scores of 70, 69 and 69 through three.After a disastrous 2-over 74 in the second round, top-ranked Scheffler tied Young for a Saturday best of 65. With a strong final day and some luck in the field, the U.S. stalwart can capture his third Masters. He won it all in 2022 and 2024; the even-year magic could be in effect as the tournament hits its homestretch.Leaderboard through SaturdayPositionPlayerTotalT1Cameron Young-11T1Rory McIlroy-113Sam Burns-104Shane Lowry-9T5Jason Day-8T5Justin Rose-8T7Scottie Scheffler-7T7Haotong Li-7T9Patrick Cantlay-6T9Russell Henley-6T9Patrick Reed-6Last 10 Masters winners2025: Rory McIlroy 2024: Scottie Scheffler 2023: Jon Rahm 2022: Scottie Scheffler 2021: Hideki Matsuyama 2020: Dustin Johnson 2019: Tiger Woods 2018: Patrick Reed 2017: Sergio Garcia 2016: Danny WillettUpdated Masters oddsStreaming links in this article are provided by partners of The Athletic.
